translation_direction: ja → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Japanese electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Discrepancies between testimonies (number of arrows, times, the horse’s whereabouts, who killed the husband) are rendered exactly and never harmonised.
decisions.rationale: The story’s meaning depends on irreconcilable accounts.

decisions.decision: Woodcutter Dạ, thưa quan; monk bần tăng; freed convict Bẩm quan; old woman già này; Tajōmaru tôi/các ông; the woman tôi and thiếp/chàng; the ghost ta.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: 丈は四寸 (conventional horse height, 4 shaku 4 sun ≈ 1.3 m) had become a horse about 40 cm tall; now ‘chừng một mét ba’.
行腳 misspelt hành khước (‘refuse’); corrected to hành cước.
The husband walks beside the mounted wife, and the route is the monk’s own; いえ as à không.
Headings made parallel: the five 物語 as Lời kể … khi bị quan Kebiishi tra hỏi; 放免 as người phóng miễn.
お死になすって下さい no longer sounds like a curse: xin chàng cũng hãy chết theo thiếp; 合 as hợp (5.12); naturalness fixes in 3.2, 4.2, a stage direction in 7.4 and 7.8; dashes normalised.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: One term throughout and in the title; the idiomatic sense of 藪の中 (‘the truth cannot be known’) has no Vietnamese equivalent.

glossary.draft_rendering: Lời kể … khi bị quan Kebiishi tra hỏi / Lời thú tội / Lời sám hối
glossary.rationale: Parallel headings follow the source’s own three genres of testimony.
The husband’s and Tajōmaru’s robes are kept distinct in every testimony.

witness_decision: Selected the Aozora Bunko transcription (card 179, file 179_15255) of 芥川龍之介全集4 (ちくま文庫, 1987), in modern orthography. The testimony headings are kept as text because they identify each speaker. First published in 新潮, January 1922; not collated.

unresolved_questions.explanation: Trong lùm cây matches the body term, but lùm cây suggests a smaller clump than 藪, and the idiom’s sense of unknowable truth is lost.

title_review.rationale: Trong lùm cây renders 藪の中 literally and matches the body term; Vietnamese cannot carry the idiomatic sense of an unknowable truth.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Compared the four witnesses’ testimonies to the magistrate.
Compared the woman’s repentance, the ghost’s account and the dateline.
